description.text: Leonardo DRS, Inc. provides advanced defense technology to U.S. national security customers and allied defense forces worldwide. We specialize in the design, development, manufacture, and integration of advanced sensing, network computing, force protection, and electric power and propulsion technologies and solutions. As a mid-sized defense technology company, our combination of operational speed and agility, deep domain expertise, and established positions on priority defense platforms has resulted in a durable and diversified portfolio of programs across the DoW. We believe DRS is well positioned to support current operational requirements, while facilitating the DoW’s rapid transition toward more autonomous, software-enabled, interconnected, and multi-domain capabilities required to address increasingly complex and proliferating threats. Enhancements in sensing, artificial intelligence (“AI”)-enabled computing, self-protection, and power generation and management are central to these priorities. Demand for our technologies is concentrated in areas of sustained priority for the DoW, including counter-unmanned aircraft systems (“C-UAS”), advanced infrared sensing, network computing, and electric power and propulsion for next generation navy vessels.

about.description_short: Leonardo DRS, Inc. (Nasdaq: DRS) is at the forefront of developing transformative defense technologies using its proven agility and delivering innovative solutions for U.S. national security customers and allies worldwide. We specialize in rapidly providing high-performance, multi-domain capabilities across next-generation advanced sensing, network computing, force protection, and electric power and propulsion. Our reputation as a trusted provider is built on a continuous focus on practical innovation, delivering quality, and meeting our customers' most demanding mission requirements. For further information on our complete range of capabilities, visit www.LeonardoDRS.com.

analysis_md:
# DRS — Leonardo DRS, Inc.
Pass-1 run, 2026-10-20, engine release 5.5.0. Price $35.18 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap $9.453B — in scope under $40B.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed.

## What it is
US defense electronics subsidiary of Italy's Leonardo S.p.A. (~72% owner; DRS listed on Nasdaq in November 2022 after the RADA merger). Two segments: Advanced Sensing and Computing (tactical radar, electro-optical/infrared sensing, tactical computing/networking) and Integrated Mission Systems (naval electric power and propulsion — including Columbia-class — and force protection). SIC 3812. Revenue FY2025 $3,648M, +12.8% YoY (latest rev YoY, key_numbers.md growth components).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $366M; capex $139.0M (rollup: PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, key_numbers.md); SBC $32M (ShareBasedCompensation).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $195.0M = $0.73/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE total $195.0M, latest FY OE/share $0.73).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC, financials_history.csv): $278M total for FY2025 — above the conservative figure because capex ($139M) exceeded D&A ($93M in the CSV) and ΔNWC was $0; the conservative OCF-based figure is the one used throughout.
- OE positive 4 of the last 5 fiscal years: FY2022 was the negative year (OCF collapsed to $33M in the CSV, the RADA-merger / working-capital year), which is why the 3-yr median ($0.61) sits below the latest FY.
- Net debt (latest): **−$300.0M** (net cash; key_numbers.md). Net debt / normalized OE −0.90x (key_numbers.md diagnostics).

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $366,000,000 − prior YTD −$166,000,000 + current YTD −$31,000,000 = **TTM $501,000,000** (H1 OCF is seasonally negative both years; the TTM improvement is the H1 loss narrowing by $135M plus the strong H2 2025)
- Capex: FY $139,000,000 − prior YTD $60,000,000 + current YTD $59,000,000 = **TTM $138,000,000**
- SBC: FY $32,000,000 − prior YTD $14,000,000 + current YTD $11,000,000 = **TTM $29,000,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **268,700,000**
- **TTM OE total $334,000,000 → base OE/share $1.24** (base_source: ttm_json; key_numbers.md base OE/share $1.24)
- The engine's normalized base (3-yr median) is $0.61/share and the latest FY is $0.73/share. The TTM base is used per the STALE_FY procedure, but it is the generous end of the range — defense OCF is H2-weighted and lumpy, and the TTM figure is ~2x the median. The method range below therefore matters more than the headline: on the median base the preliminary run printed weighted IRR 4.93% and IV@15 $6.41 (dcf_numbers.json of the preliminary run, superseded). Either way the tier is D.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate / narrow
Justification: embedded incumbent positions on long-lived US platforms with real qualification and switching barriers, but mid-tier scale, hardware margins, and ROIC that has only just cleared the cost of capital.
- FOR: Embedded incumbent on long-lived platforms (Columbia-class electric propulsion, tactical radar, EO/IR) — qualification and switching costs are high; record funded backlog $5.1B at Q2 2026 (+17% YoY, 8-K filed 2026-07-30), ~1.4x revenue, with book-to-bill 1.2x and 18 consecutive quarters at or above 1.0; gross margin expanding steadily — 16.9% (FY2019) to 23.8% (FY2025) per fundamentals.json; net cash balance sheet (net debt −$300M at FY2025) funds capacity expansion and M&A without leverage.
- AGAINST: Mid-tier scale vs RTX and L3Harris — smaller R&D and program-capture resources than the primes; **ROIC evidence (fundamentals.json roic_proxy): 8.9% FY2023, 10.2% FY2024, 11.8% FY2025** (FY2022's 19.5% is the merger-year outlier, operating margin 20.8% that year vs 8-10% around it) — returns sit just above the cost of capital, not at wide-moat levels, and gross margin is ~23%; single-customer concentration (US DoD budgets, continuing resolutions, program timing); Leonardo S.p.A. owns ~72% — minority float is thin and parent interests govern; capex stepping up (FY2025 $139M vs $85M FY2024; management guides capex at mid-4% of revenue) and the announced $450M all-cash Raft acquisition (Q2 2026) consume the cash the OE base generates.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-20)
Growth sanity check: the engine's blended start is 6.72% (components: rev CAGR 5y 5.60%, rev CAGR 3y 10.64%, latest rev YoY 12.80%, OE/share CAGR 2y 22.37%, share-count adjustment −5.00pp applied to the revenue components). Recent prints run hotter — Q2 2026 revenue +10.1% YoY and management reconfirmed FY2026 revenue guidance of $3.9-3.975B (+7-9% organic) while raising adjusted EPS guidance to $1.34-$1.39 (8-K, 2026-07-30). The base start of 6.7% sits slightly **below** those prints, deliberately: the guidance is a revenue figure, while OE growth must absorb the capex step-up to mid-4% of revenue and Raft integration; the bull (11.7%) and super-bull (18.7%) starts sit above the latest prints, so the upside cases are not capped below what the company just printed. Default probabilities 10/25/30/25/10 and default OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25 kept — no company-specific evidence justifies skewing them. Price $35.18.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | -5.3% | 0.75 | Budget/CR disruption, program slips, TTM OCF proves to be timing | $5.52 | 4.27% |
| Bear | 25% | 1.7% | 0.90 | Growth stalls at low-single digits; capex stays elevated | $8.88 | 5.63% |
| Base | 30% | 6.7% | 1.00 | Guided trajectory decays over the CAP | $12.15 | 6.96% |
| Bull | 25% | 11.7% | 1.10 | Backlog converts at recent-print growth; margins keep expanding | $16.42 | 8.65% |
| Super bull | 10% | 18.7% | 1.25 | Counter-UAS/radar volume (e.g. 50,000-unit camera-core orders) scales like a production franchise | $24.80 | 11.70% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $13.00 (−63.0% vs price), IV@12% $17.39, IV@10% $22.31, weighted IRR 7.34%, base-case IRR 6.96%** (key_numbers.md)
- **Tier by numbers: D** — bear and bull tiers are both D (IRR band bear 5.63% → bull 8.65%); even the super-bull scenario (11.70%) does not reach the 15% hurdle.
- Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 3.53% (on the TTM base), terminal value 19.4% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.49x, net debt −0.90x normalized OE, 9.6 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path): 15% at $13.00 · 20% at $9.07 · 25% at $6.92.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q2 2026, legs quoted above. Caveat recorded with it: the TTM base ($1.24) is ~2x the 3-yr median ($0.61) because defense OCF is H2-weighted and H1 2026's OCF loss narrowed sharply vs H1 2025; the verdict does not depend on the choice (Tier D on both bases — see method range).
- **DILUTION** (share count growing 7.7%/yr): the CAGR is an artifact of the window straddling the November 2022 RADA merger share issuance — diluted shares in financials_history.csv run 215,100,000 (FY2022) → 264,200,000 (FY2023) → 267,700,000 (FY2024) → 268,700,000 (FY2025), i.e. ~0.8%/yr since the merger, not 7.7%. The engine's −5.00pp growth adjustment therefore over-penalizes the revenue components; it is left in place (conservative direction, and the tier is D with or without it). SBC trend checked: $17M (FY2023) → $22M (FY2024) → $32M (FY2025) in the CSV, $29M TTM — rising but ~9% of TTM OE; fundamentals.json shows TTM buybacks of $37M against $11M issuance, so the count is now roughly flat-to-shrinking.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 4.49x super-bear IV): real — the outcome range is genuinely wide because the price capitalizes a growth path the OE base does not yet fund. Confidence is set to **low**, and the verdict is sized to the conservative end.
- **Share basis (informational, key_numbers.md):** in-history split facts dated 2021-02-28 and 2022-11-23, ratio 1.45135 (the RADA-merger-era recapitalization), both on or before the latest FY end and never applied by the engine. Checked against financials_history.csv: no share-count jump of ~1.45x appears inside the last four years (215.1M → 264.2M → 267.7M → 268.7M; the one jump is the merger issuance above), so DILUTION and the share adjustment are not split artifacts beyond what is already noted.
- The preliminary run's **LOW_OE_YIELD** flag (1.7% on the median base) dropped off the final run because the TTM base yields 3.53% — noted here so the disappearance is explained: on either base the yield is thin and the valuation rests on growth the model cannot verify; that fragility stands.

## Data / enrichment notes
- No overrides of any kind; no DATA_GAP. Capex is a single filed rollup tag every year (PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment), no intangibles leg, no CAPEX_COVERAGE_LOW flag (capex $139M vs D&A $93M in FY2025).
- Enrichment all ran: fundamentals.json, prices.json (daily series complete; the intraday chart request failed — non-blocking), segments.json, statements.json, profile.json + street.json (Street consensus Buy, n=6, target $51.57 per profile.py output — the Street is pricing the growth path the OE model rejects; that gap is the finding, not a data error), live.json (live price $35.18, live IRR 7.34%, tier D — unchanged from scored).

## My thoughts / method range
- The honest headline is the range: median base → weighted IRR 4.93%, IV@15 $6.41; TTM base → 7.34%, $13.00. Both are Tier D by a wide margin, and even the super-bull case on the generous base (11.70%) misses 15%. At $35.18 the market is paying ~28x TTM owner's earnings (price ÷ base OE/share $1.24) for a business earning ~10-12% ROIC — the price assumes the backlog converts into durably higher OE than any filed year has yet produced.
- Quality is real but mid-tier: backlog visibility is excellent ($5.1B funded, 18 straight quarters of book-to-bill ≥1.0), margins are expanding, and the balance sheet is net cash even before the $450M Raft deal. None of that is in dispute — the dispute is only the price.
- Risks to the D verdict (i.e. what would make it too harsh): sustained double-digit OE growth if radar/counter-UAS volumes scale production-style, Raft proving immediately accretive, or a Leonardo take-private / float event re-rating the minority stub. Risks the other way: the TTM OCF improvement reversing as working-capital timing, capex staying at mid-4%+ of revenue, and DoD budget disruption.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 7.34% on the TTM base; 4.93% on the median base — D either way)
- Confidence: **Low** (WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD plus a base that moves 2x between the median and TTM definitions; the tier itself is robust to that uncertainty)
- One-liner: Solid mid-tier defense franchise, moat 5/10 — does not clear 15% at $35.18 on any scenario (weighted IRR 7.3% on the TTM base, IV@15 $13.00); it would need to fall to ~$13 to clear the 15% hurdle.
